title: Draw a hexagon
prompt:
The starter draws a square. Change it to draw a hexagon: six sides of 100 steps each, with the turtle back where it started at the end.

Run `python3 hexagon.py` to see your drawing in a window. The tests use a stand-in turtle that writes down every move, so they run even on a computer without Tk.
hints: Two numbers change: how many times the loop runs, and how far the turtle turns at each corner.
To get back where it started, the turtle turns all the way round once in total: 360 degrees shared among six corners.
`for side in range(6):` with `turtle.forward(100)` and `turtle.left(60)` inside.
explain_after: `forward(d)` moves the turtle and `left(a)` turns it by degrees [py-069]. Six turns of 60 degrees add up to one full turn, so the turtle ends facing the way it started. `turtle.done()` stays last so the window stays open [py-070].
